MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Department - Program 


Join Monash Health as a Quality Systems & Insights Analyst and play a key role in improving the safety and quality of care for one of Victoria's largest health services. Combining data analytics, quality systems expertise and clinical governance insight, you'll transform information into meaningful action, support organisation wide quality systems, and help leaders make decisions that improve patient outcomes. If you enjoy solving problems, working with data, optimising systems, and partnering with stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and positive change, this is an opportunity to make a real impact across a complex and dynamic healthcare environment.


The Quality & Clinical Governance Unit plays a central role in supporting Monash Health's commitment to delivering safe, effective and high-quality care. The team provides leadership, systems and oversight that strengthen clinical governance, quality improvement, patient safety and organisational learning across the health service.


The Quality Insights & Systems team manages and optimises key quality systems, supports the collection and analysis of clinical governance information, and provides meaningful insights that help leaders identify risks, monitor performance and drive continuous improvement. Working collaboratively with programs and services across Monash Health, the team supports evidence-based decision-making and initiatives that enhance patient outcomes and organisational performance.







About the Role 








This is a part time ongoing position located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, you will work under the leadership of the Quality Insights & Systems manager and collaborate closely with the broader Quality & Clinical Governance team and stakeholders across Monash Health.


This is an exciting opportunity for a quality systems and data professional who enjoys combining analytical thinking, systems administration and continuous improvement to support safer patient care. The role is responsible for maintaining and optimising key organisational quality systems while developing meaningful clinical governance insights that inform decision-making and improvement initiatives.










Key responsibilities include:



Administering and optimising Monash Health's quality systems, including incident management, document control and audit platforms.


Analysing clinical quality data and other information sources to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement. 


Developing and delivering clinical governance reports, dashboards and insights that support leaders and teams. 


Providing user support, education and training to improve staff capability in quality systems and data interpretation. 


Working with internal stakeholders, external vendors and partner teams to enhance system performance, data integrity and governance processes. 


Contributing to quality improvement initiatives, system enhancements and process optimisation projects.









This role will involve working with stakeholders across multiple Monash Health sites. A hybrid working arrangement may be available in line with team and organisational requirements.







About You 


To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring demonstrated experience in systems administration, data analysis and quality improvement within a complex organisational environment. 


You will be someone who is curious, analytical and solutions-focused, with the ability to translate data into meaningful insights and build strong collaborative relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.


You will have:




Experience administering, supporting or improving systems and processes in a complex organisation. 


Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and communicate actionable insights. 


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including report writing, presentations and development of guidance materials.


Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building capabilities. 


Experience providing education, training and support to end-users.


High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining data integrity and quality. 


Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset. 


Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.


Experience using RiskMan, PROMPT, MARS or similar systems will be highly regarded.



Mandatory Requirements:




Degree qualification in health, quality, business management, data analytics or a related discipline.


Current right to work in Australia. 


Ability to obtain and maintain required screening checks, including National Police Check and Working with Children Check.


Current Victorian Driver's Licence is highly desirable



 
Desirable:




Knowledge of quality, safety and clinical governance principles within a health service environment. 


Experience working in a complex healthcare organisation.This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to Monash Health's quality and safety agenda, helping to strengthen systems, generate valuable organisational insights and support continuous improvement across one of Australia's largest health services. 










For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Linda Chuang, Qualtiy Insights & Systems Manager via linda.chuang@monashhealth.org

02 Jul 2026 to 03 Aug 2026

PROCUREMENT MANAGER
MUDEX 
CANNING VALE, WA 6155
EMPLOYMENT TYPE: FULL-TIME PERMANENT
SALARY: $110,000 TO $140,000 YEARLY
	
Purpose of role             
As a Procurement Specialist, you will be responsible for national procurement activities, processes, and sourcing of goods and services for the business to ensure the continuous supply and availability of materials whilst complying with planning and control system expectations. You will ensure products and services are delivered within timeframes and at the most cost-effective price to meet or exceed internal and external customer expectations. The role will have key interactions with other teams to standardize process and strategic business planning.
 
Main duties and responsibilities
             
Core objectives include: 
 
•	Assisting in production planning and scheduling of work orders
•	Monitoring sales data and stock levels
•	Studying trade, manufacturers, and market information to keep informed of changing market conditions
•	Negotiating purchase and supply arrangements with suppliers
•	Assisting in designing and implementing pricing by monitoring and updating cost of goods
•	Liaising with management on long-term purchasing planning
•	Establishing working plans according to seasonal and budgetary requirements
•	Anticipating customer trends and determining quantity and quality of goods to be purchased
•	Inspecting, comparing, and selecting raw materials by quality and specifications
•	Receiving samples from raw material and packaging suppliers
•	Researching and evaluating potential suppliers
•	Comparing and evaluating offers from suppliers
•	Negotiating contract terms of agreement and pricing
•	Tracking orders and ensuring timely delivery
•	Reviewing quality of purchased products
•	Entering order details regarding suppliers, quantities, prices into internal warehouse management database
•	Maintaining updated records of purchased products, delivery information and invoices
•	Preparing reports on purchases, including cost analysis
•	Monitoring stock levels and place orders as needed
•	Coordinating with warehouse staff to ensure proper storage
•	Following and enforcing the company’s procurement policies and procedures
•	Managing inventories and maintaining accurate purchase and pricing records
•	Maintaining and updating supplier information such as qualifications, delivery times, product ranges, etc.
•	Maintaining good supplier relations and negotiating contracts

The above list is not exhaustive, and the role may change to meet the overall objectives of the company.

Other duties     
As required by management and other department personnel as requested / required.
              

PERSON SPECIFICATION
 
Qualifications 

•	Degree level (desirable) or formal qualifications in procurement is well regarded 

Experience

•	5+ years of Purchasing / Procurement / Supply planning experience required
•	Ability to build strong internal and external business relationships
•	Experience dealing with and managing International Suppliers required
•	Proven ability to build strong internal and external business relationships
•	Demonstrated experience in developing supplier relationships with a focus on supplier performance
•	Experience with Warehouse Management and Enterprise Resource Planning systems 
•	Proficient user of Xero Accounting Software & Microsoft Office Applications
•	Well-developed analytical skills
•	Experienced in creating financial reports and contract cost analysis
              
Skills & competencies  
 
•	Attention to detail: excellent attention to detail and written skills when communicating with others, both internally and externally.
•	Commerciality: ability to apply knowledge in a practical, commercial manner. 
•	Teamwork: willingness to assist and support others as required and get on with team members. 
•	Time management/organisation: accomplish objectives effectively within time frame given and carry out administrative duties within portfolio in an efficient and timely manner.
Personal attributes      
 
•	Professional approach
•	Ability to work under pressure
•	Excellent organisational and time management skills
•	Excellent attention to detail
•	Confident manner
•	Positive approach to change

SALARY: $110,000 TO $140,000 YEARLY

About Dipole Group
We are a wholly Australian owned and operated ICT and Telecom networks specialist delivery business. Dipole operates locally, regionally, and internationally. Our capabilities span across Telecommunications, Finance, Insurance, health, Public Services, Print / Digital Media, Broadcast and Supply Chain. Dipole Group is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

The Role
The ICT Support Engineer develops support procedures and strategies for systems, networks, operating systems and applications development. This role provides technical expertise and direction in support of system infrastructure and process improvements, diagnoses and resolves complex system problems, and ensures the delivery of high-quality 24/7 technical support services. 

Key Responsibilities:
•	Diagnose and resolve complex technical problems related to hardware, software, networks, and systems infrastructure, including installation, maintenance, repair, upgrade, and configuration of desktops, servers, email, databases, operating systems, and security systems.
•	Develop and implement support procedures and strategies for systems, networks, operating systems, and applications development, defining escalation, response, and resolution timeframes based on criticality and impact.
•	Prioritise and triage incoming incidents and service requests to ensure timely response and appropriate escalation, managing Incident and Change queues to ensure service restoration and completion within agreed SLAs.
•	Act as the primary escalation point of contact for onshore and offshore teams, managing High Impact Incidents across affected lines of business and driving restoration within agreed timeframes.
•	Test, identify, and diagnose functionality errors and faults in systems and programming code within established testing protocols, guidelines, and quality standards to ensure systems perform to specification.
•	Perform organisational systems architecture reviews and assessments, recommending current and future hardware and software strategies and directions to facilitate business growth and agility.
•	Develop, conduct, and provide technical guidance and training in application software and operational procedures for team members, ensuring continuous upskilling and knowledge transfer.
•	Create and review technical documentation such as procedural, instructional, and operational guides, technical reports, specifications, and maintenance inventory systems.
•	Schedule and conduct quality audit inspections, analysing and reviewing systems, data, and documentation to identify variations and potential high-risk areas in securing adherence to standards and procedures.
•	Recommend corrective action plans and improvements in the resolution of non-compliance with standards detected through monitoring and auditing of processes and procedures.
•	Communicate, educate, and liaise with users and management to ensure awareness and adherence to standards, procedures, and quality control issues, while interacting with clients to determine satisfaction levels and areas of potential dissatisfaction.
•	Lead infrastructure projects as Project Manager, monitoring and controlling project time, cost, quality, and risks throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring all business and technical requirements are met.
